subject: 🏃 Wednesday — Heavy Strength (Wk 7, Presidio Pivot Week)
html:
Tomorrow: Heavy Strength at Cañada College. This is structural insurance for the knee and hips heading into Sunday's Presidio HM pivot test — maintain load, no progression. Hold all working weights; this is not a PR day.

Warm-up: Foam roll quads/IT band (1 min each) → glute bridges (10 reps) → quadruped hip CARs (3 each leg) → bodyweight squats (10 reps) → RDL pattern with empty bar (10 reps).

The session:

  • Back squat: 165 lb, 4×6, 3-sec eccentric. Hips break first, knees track over toes. Held at 165 (backed off from 175 — the one session at 175 was the only 2/5 knee reading of the block).
  • Romanian deadlift: 165 lb, 4×6 — bring straps. Hinge, neutral spine, hamstring stretch. Without straps, grip fails by set 4.
  • Standing calf raise: 155 lb back-rack barbell, 4×10. Full ROM (heel below step), 2-sec hold at top, 3-sec lower. Do it in the rack with safeties set.
  • Reverse Nordic: Bodyweight, 3×10. Kneel on pad, knees hip-width, glutes squeezed, 3-sec lower. Continue building depth — stop on any sharp PF pain.

Focus cue: Smooth, controlled eccentrics — especially on the squat. You ran a clean 3×1600m sharpener yesterday (all reps 7:06–7:09 at HR 155–158, knee 1/5), so expect the legs to be a touch heavy from the Tue-run/Wed-lift split. That's normal. If anything feels off in the knee, hold load or cut the session — protecting Sunday is the priority.

Where you are: Week 7 of 12, Phase 2. 4 days to the Presidio Half Marathon pivot test (June 21). The three gates: sub-1:37:30 finish, avg HR <170 final 3 mi, zero knee compensation. The knee has been 1/5 for every V6 session except one (Jun 3 stairs, which is why squat backed off to 165). Tomorrow's lift keeps the structural insurance current without costing freshness. Thu is a 6-mi progression run, Fri stability lift, Sat full rest, then the gated test Sunday.

Tonight: Pack your gym bag (don't forget the straps), set the alarm, bed by 10. Quick session, in and out — save the intensity for Sunday.
